analysis: What changed since Thursday's 9:00 AM PT post-open brief: the selloff fully matured into the close - Nasdaq -2.60% (worst since June), S&P -1.21% (worst since July), META down 7.13% to $648.76 shedding ~$124B, and the 10Y posted its largest one-day drop in 3+ years to 4.961% as money fled to safety. Thursday evening's main new datapoint is WDC's print: a clean beat ($4.64 vs $4.11) plus a raised guide ($5.80 Q2 EPS vs ~$4.84) trading down ~4.4% after hours - the LRCX template confirmed, the market now demands demand proof beyond the guide. Signal vs noise: the META FCF reversal (-$2.12B, first outflow ever) plus $825B in lease commitments is signal - it is the defining repricing of the whole AI trade, and the WSB community read (via sellthenews, 1500 comments overnight) agrees the question flipped from 'what AI earns' to 'what AI costs'. The Iran-strike oil bid and the Anthropic S-1 timing remain single-source noise until confirmed. The bright spots - AAPL +1.28%, DIA/IWM flat, the defensive rotation - show this is crowded-AI deleveraging, not a broad collapse; futures stabilizing overnight (+0.18% Nasdaq) is consistent with that. The next catalyst stack is crowded: Anthropic S-1 today, flash PMI/Michigan mid-morning, then the Oct 28 mega-earnings cluster (GOOGL/MSFT/AMZN) and the Oct 27-28 Fed meeting.

community_signals.takeaway: Near-capitulation on the AI trade but not the broad index: consensus is the market now prices capex and free cash flow, not revenue/EPS - META's $825B in lease commitments and first negative FCF are the emblem; $650 is the community's line in the sand. Fear/greed low but VIX still under 20 - bears call SPY 'an ant-sized pullback' off the ATH, framing it as crowded-AI deleveraging. Hope is pinned on WDC's print and Friday's tape.

headlines.headline: Futures mixed after the Nasdaq's worst day since June: Dow futures -0.38%, S&P 500 futures -0.06%, Nasdaq futures +0.18% (Seeking Alpha, ~1:09 AM PT). Thursday's close: S&P 500 -1.21%, Nasdaq -2.60%, Dow roughly flat; bond yields fell as investors fled to safety, 10-year at 4.961% (-18.5 bps).
headlines.why_it_matters: A stabilization attempt, but only Nasdaq futures are green and the levels are razor-thin - watch whether futures hold or fade into the opening auction. The bond bid is fear, not growth optimism.

headlines.headline: Western Digital beat big: fiscal Q1 adjusted EPS $4.64 vs $4.11 consensus (Zacks $4.09), revenue $4.381B (+55% YoY) vs $4.14B est, gross margin 58.1%, dividend raised 17% to $0.175; Q2 guide EPS $5.80 +/- $0.20 on $5.0-5.2B revenue, far above ~$4.84/$4.57B expectations. Shares still traded down ~4.4% in extended trading (~$338.72 vs $354.19 close, per MarketBeat).
headlines.why_it_matters: The LRCX template holds: a beat plus a raise is not enough - the stock is being priced against AI-storage perfection. Memory names (MU, SNDK, STX) will read WDC's guide, not its beat. After-hours quote single-source via MarketBeat - treat that leg as fragile.

headlines.headline: META closed -7.13% at $648.76, shedding ~$124B of market cap, after disclosing ~$825B in future lease commitments and noncancelable contracts (up from ~$700B in July) alongside its first-ever quarterly free-cash-flow outflow (-$2.12B vs +$10.63B a year ago). Q3 revenue $64.6B (+26% vs $63.4B est), adjusted EPS $7.40 vs $6.52 est; AI capex was $34.91B in the quarter and the 2026 guide's lower bound was raised to $135-145B. Non-voting share plan still looms.
headlines.why_it_matters: The tape has moved from 'who grows in AI' to 'who pays for AI' - a clean revenue/EPS beat cannot carry negative FCF and a dilution vehicle. $650 is the community's line in the sand into Friday.

headlines.headline: TSLA beat on the quarter (adjusted EPS $0.48 vs $0.43 expected, revenue $28.05B) but faded after cutting its annual capital expenditure forecast; GAAP net income fell 43% to $787M. Analyst targets now span $157 (HSBC Reduce) to $480 (RBC Buy). SpaceX fully round-tripped its own earnings pop (-9.03%).
headlines.why_it_matters: The market read the capex cut as a slower autonomy/robotics pace - the exact 'who pays for the buildout' question now hitting the whole AI complex. The intraday recovery read as merger-arb rotation, not conviction.

headlines.headline: The Mag 7 wrap: NVDA -4.4%, GOOGL -3.2% (below its 200-day), AMZN -3.9% on Thursday, all pulled into the capex repricing; AAPL +1.28% at $348.34 was the safe haven as 'not burning money on AI'. GOOGL, MSFT and AMZN all report Oct 28, one mega-earnings day.
headlines.why_it_matters: Oct 28 is the next checkpoint - the tape trades capex guidance now, not prints, so each hyperscaler's AI spend number matters more than its revenue beat. AAPL's green day shows where money hides.

headlines.headline: Anthropic S-1 watch: no filing on EDGAR as of ~4:05 AM PT (checked directly). The Yahoo Finance three-source report - that Anthropic could publicly file its S-1 as early as Friday, clearing the 15-day runway for a November listing - has now been syndicated by Seeking Alpha, PYMNTS and Invezz. WSJ-reported S-1 figures: $16.3B H1 revenue against a >$80B net loss; valuation chatter has slipped toward ~$1.5T from ~$2T.
headlines.why_it_matters: A confirmed filing would drop AI unit economics - $72B in non-cash charges, $518B+ in compute commitments - straight into an AI-spending selloff. Single-source on the timing - treat as fragile until EDGAR shows it.

headlines.headline: Oil holds the energy bid: WTI ~$100.37 (+0.89%), Brent ~$113.98 (+0.67%) in early trading, near five-month highs, on Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and the unconfirmed NYT report of planned U.S.-Israel strikes on Iran after the Nov 3 midterms.
headlines.why_it_matters: Energy is the one real hedge - crude is now the macro risk factor into year-end, and costlier energy tightens the Fed's room ahead of next week's meeting. The strike-planning cause is unconfirmed - the bid can fade fast.
